notes: v1.14.581 — ONE ENGINE FOR "HOW MANY RACKS", AND --tac FINALLY EXISTS. Two owner-ruled fixes. Q-b: --tac was referenced by THREE declarations on the OPS wall — the cell border, the :active border and the .oc-n label colour — and declared NOWHERE. No stylesheet, no element, no setProperty. Under Contract 15 an undefined var() invalidates the WHOLE declaration silently, so all three were dead and the wall had been rendering without its accent since the cells shipped. The note at :8910 asserts the opposite, that --tac is set inline per cell so nothing can silently die there; that inline write was never implemented. A comment is not a declaration, and this is the exact mock-token trap that same note was written to warn about. Declared on the cell rather than :root so a future inline per-cell accent still wins. Q-c: Command answered "how many racks" TWICE. The hero counted the ACTIVE deployment and the KPI/stat cells summed rack rows across EVERY deployment, so a torture Master read "0 racks on US-TST99. Tap one." beside a cell reading 60 — and NEITHER number was the Master's. Owner ruling: the cells show the MASTER rack count, the hero names the deployment state. Both surfaces now call one function, cmd_masterRackCount(). THE HEADLINE KEEPS "Tap one" — the .573 contract pairs that promise with the picker CTA and this file already took a device fail over breaking that pairing. THE DEEPER CAUSE IS REMOVED, NOT JUST THE SYMPTOM: the hero's count came from deploy_getActiveId() while the headline's very existence is gated by nowtab_resolveDep() — two engines for "which deployment is active" that can disagree, which is how a device holding 60 racks could read zero. Deleting the count deletes the divergence. The deployment-scoped rackCount still drives rung and the NBA: this ruling governs what the surfaces SAY, not where the shift is routed.
